1.why: The reset token digest is stored on and validated against the requesting session only, so cross-session reuse is impossible, but the app has no user store at all and never associates the token with the submitted contact/identity, so 'belongs to the user' is only partially true.

2.why: A token can only be verified against `session.recovery.tokenDigest` of the very session that requested it, so the same code cannot work for any other session/user.

3.why: There is no session invalidation or ID rotation after `/api/recovery/password` succeeds — the same `recovery_session` cookie stays valid and simply advances to the next stage — although the demo has no concept of other logged-in sessions to invalidate.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured TLS-only with cert/key, non-HTTPS is rejected, and HSTS plus `upgrade-insecure-requests` are set; however no minimum TLS version/cipher policy is explicitly pinned (it relies on Bun defaults, which are TLS 1.2/1.3).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests and compared in constant time, and passwords are hashed with bcrypt cost 12; no other user data is stored, though nothing is actually encrypted at rest.

6.why: No email is ever generated or sent — delivery is simulated by returning `testResetToken`/`testMfaCode` directly in the HTTP JSON response and printing them in the page, so there is no email message guarding private data.

7.why: Request bodies must be JSON objects, fields are type-checked (`typeof body.token === 'string'`), lengths/policy are enforced server-side, `escapeHtml` is applied to injected page values, and client rendering uses `textContent` only; the contact value is never stored or reflected.

8.why: There are no server- or client-side redirects; navigation is purely local hash routing and CSP sets `form-action 'self'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `default-src 'none'`, so no off-site destinations are reachable.

9.why: There are no email templates in the codebase at all, so while no user-supplied HTML/script can appear in an email, the statement cannot be positively verified for this system.

10.why: The live reset token and MFA code are returned in API responses and explicitly written to the browser console and the visible `#logs` panel via `mockLog`, so secrets are shown in logs (error responses themselves are generic and leak nothing).

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and tokens hashed, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in source as `session.mfaCode = "482913"`, i.e. a secret code embedded in the code.

12.why: The fixed, source-embedded MFA code `482913` functions as a default credential that any user can supply, even though there are no default admin accounts or default passwords.

13.why: Both a per-session `throttled()` bucket and a bounded per-trusted-IP `ipThrottled()` bucket cap request/verify/password/MFA attempts (3–5 per 10 minutes) and return HTTP 429.

14.why: `/api/recovery/request` always returns the same neutral message ('If the contact can be used for recovery…') and the contact value is never validated, stored, or reflected, so existence is never disclosed.

15.why: The token is `randomBytes(32)` base64url, single-use, 10-minute TTL, and bound to the issuing session, so it is random and complex; 'user-specific' holds only in the session sense since no user identities exist.
